articles.title: Kremlin says PM Modi, Xi offered Putin their 'good offices' to help end Ukraine war
articles.summary: India News: Russia on Sunday said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping offered their services to help end the Ukraine war on the sid.
articles.body: Russia on Sunday said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping offered their services to help end the Ukraine war on the sidelines of the Brics summit.According to news agency Reuters, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said that Russian President Vladimir Putin welcomed their readiness.“During their bilateral meetings, Modi and Xi took a keen interest in the Ukraine settlement and actively offered their good offices to help find a solution,” Peskov said.This comes amid US President Donald Trump's ongoing efforts to broker a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine.PM Modi and Putin also held a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the summit and discussed closer trade ties, including implementation of the Programme for Economic Cooperation 2030, as well as cooperation in infrastructure, energy, technology, defence and culture.They had earlier met on the sidelines of the Shanghai cooperation organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek on August 31.“Delighted to meet President Putin in Delhi, less than two weeks after our meeting in Bishkek. During today’s meeting, we talked about closer trade ties, including implementation of the Programme for Economic Cooperation 2030. Cooperation in areas like infrastructure, energy, technology, defence, culture and more," PM Modi said in a post on X.India’s efforts during our Brics presidency aimed at furthering the welfare of our planet,” he added.According to the ministry of external affairs, the two leaders also exchanged views on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, including conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region, which have affected maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers.PM Modi reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy remain the way forward in resolving conflicts and said India stands ready to assist in peace efforts.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Congress doing politics over food served to Brics leaders': BJP targets Rahul Gandhi after '80% non-veg' post
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday took a swipe at the all-vegetarian menu served at the Bric.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday took a swipe at the all-vegetarian menu served at the Brics Summit gala dinner, saying that “80% of Indians are non-vegetarian”, while Union minister Kiren Rijiju accused the Congress of politicising the food served to the visiting leaders.Sharing a picture of Chole Bhature, Rahul in a social media post said, “For the record: 80% of Indians are non-vegetarian. Indian non-vegetarian food is delicious. As are my sister's chole bhature."Rahul's remarks came a day after an elaborate vegetarian spread was served at a gala dinner hosted during the Brics Summit. The menu featured dishes representing different regional cuisines from across India.Without naming any specific leader, Rijiju criticised the Congress over the remarks, saying the party was making an issue out of the food served to leaders of BRICS nations.“I can't believe that Congress party is making politics even on the food menu served to the leaders of BRICS nations. Our guests relished Indian vegetarian cuisine which are rich in flavor and nutritional variety with diverse regional traditions,” Rijiju said.What was served at the Brics gala dinner?The dinner began with starters including ‘Khandvi mille’, a steamed gram-flour roll tempered with mustard, coconut and curry leaves, and ‘Khumb galouti’, pan-grilled mushroom kebabs served with mint pearls.The main course featured ‘Paneer Lababdar’, ‘Gucchi Marmik’, made with Himalayan morel mushrooms and tender asparagus, and ‘Carrot Bean Poriyal’.The spread also included ‘Thakkali Belle Saaru’, a light lentil broth, millet pulao, beetroot raita and an assortment of Indian breads.For dessert, VVIP guests were served ‘Old Delhi fruit cream with jalebi’ and ‘Shahtoot phirni’.The gala dinner was also accompanied by a performance featuring an ensemble of more than 100 artistes, drawn largely from India as well as other Brics member countries.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Russia launches more than 450 drones in overnight attacks while Ukraine strikes oil refineries
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said during an interview on Saturday that he was willing to travel to the G20 summit in Miami to meet on the sideline...
articles.body:
Russia launched over 450 drones across Ukraine in overnight attacks, according to Ukraine's Armed Forces, while Kyiv struck oil refineries in Russia's Tatarstan, according to Russian authorities.

Russia launched 453 drones of various types across Ukraine, 409 of which were neutralised by Ukraine's Armed Forces. However, 13 locations were struck.

Multiple attacks on the city of Stryi, in the Lviv region, which borders Poland, left a multi-storey residential building, an outbuilding near a school and buildings near a railway station damaged after being struck by Russian drones.

In the city of Izyum, a 26-year-old woman died as a result of the detonation of an explosive device, according to the Head of the Kharkiv Regional Military Administration, Oleh Syniehub, while the city of Kharkiv and 15 settlements in the Kharkiv region were subjected to Russian attacks, leaving three people injured, including a 73-year-old woman, Syniehub added.

On Saturday, at least five people were injured in the region of Volyn in western Ukraine after Russian forces launched a mass attack which lasted more than four hours, according to the regional Governor Roman Romaniuk, with more than 10 drones flying in the region's airspace.

One train in Lutsk which had been evacuated was struck by debris, sparking a fire. No injuries were reported, according to the governor.

Meanwhile, two people were killed and 12 were injured following a Ukrainian drone attack which sparked a fire at an industrial facility in Nizhnekamsk, Russia's Republic of Tatarstan, home to a major oil refining and petrochemical hub, according to Russian authorities.

Ukraine Defence Intelligence also said it had struck the Slavyansk-ECO oil refinery in Slavyansk-on-Kuban in Russia's southeastern region of Krasnodar Krai, hitting a key oil-processing unit and the refinery's tank farm.

Russia and Ukraine continue to target each other's energy-related facilities ahead of the winter. While Russia has focused on Ukraine's electricity and energy, Ukraine has mainly targeted Russia's oil and gas infrastructure.

Russia says Putin meeting with Zelenskyy at G20 'impossible'

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said during an interview on Saturday that he was willing to travel to the G20 summit in Miami to meet on the sidelines with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"We have to come. We have to meet, to speak and make decisions," adding, "It's not about words. What I will tell him or what he wants to tell me, it doesn't matter. Results matter. That's it."

But Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov called that option "impossible" and said that Putin will only meet with Zelenskyy in Moscow.

Meanwhile, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said that Russia will not cease its "special military operations" in Ukraine during possible peace talks.

articles.title: Turkey detains 26 after 'family values' raids on LGBTQ+ groups
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Turkish authorities have detained 26 people and raided the offices of six LGBTQ+ associations across the country following allegations of prostitution.
articles.body: Turkish authorities have detained 26 people and raided the offices of six LGBTQ+ associations across the country following allegations of prostitution and obscenity, prosecutors said, in a crackdown the government says is aimed at protecting family values.The operations were carried out over the weekend across 12 provinces against 38 suspects, according to the Istanbul chief prosecutor's office. Authorities seized drugs, digital equipment, smuggled alcohol and a firearm during the raids.Ankara-based LGBTQ+ association Kaos GL said at least 50 activists had been detained, including more than 10 people taken from their homes in police raids. The group said authorities had also blocked access to dozens of websites and social media accounts linked to LGBTI+ organisations, activists and rights advocates.The crackdown, dubbed "My Family is Safe", comes as President Tayyip Erdogan promotes a "Decade of Family and Population" initiative aimed at addressing Turkey's falling birth rate and ageing population.The prosecutor's office said its investigation found evidence that children and underage youths were being inappropriately influenced on issues related to sexual orientation and gender identity.Turkey's justice minister Akin Gurlek said separate investigations coordinated by prosecutors in Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, Aydin and Mersin involved judicial proceedings against 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses across 15 provinces.The raids have drawn criticism from rights groups, which say Turkey has increasingly targeted the LGBTQ+ community in recent years through tougher rhetoric and restrictions."The real name of this operation is not 'My Family is Safe'; it is state-led discrimination, politics ​of fear ​and the dismantling ⁠of civil society," the Turkish Human Rights Association said on X.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: US diplomat accused of possessing indecent images of children secretly flown out of UK before police were informed: Report
articles.summary: US News: A US diplomat accused of possessing indecent images of children was secretly removed from the UK before police were informed, sparking a diplomatic controversy as investigations continue.
articles.body: A US diplomat accused of possessing indecent images of children on his phone was secretly removed from Britain and flown to the United States, with British authorities informed about the investigation only after his departure, The Telegraph reportedThe diplomat was working at the US embassy in London when American authorities allegedly searched his home in Putney on August 25. He was then taken to a US air base and flown to America as part of an ongoing investigation.American officers do not have powers of arrest in Britain, and there was reportedly no formal extradition request for the diplomat. The circumstances of his removal have prompted discussions between British officials and the US embassy.A source told The Sun that British police should have been notified when the property was searched and when the alleged material was discovered.“They should have told Scotland Yard when they carried out the raid, and certainly when they found material,” the source said.The source claimed the diplomat was taken to a US air base in a military convoy before being flown to the United States, where his brother was reportedly also under investigation.“The man may well face justice in the US but he should be before the courts here,” the source added.The Metropolitan Police said US authorities informed them on August 25 about an investigation into suspected offences in London involving indecent images of children.“We continue to liaise with them regarding this matter,” a police spokesman said.Flight data showed a Kalitta Air Boeing 747 flew from Chicago to RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire on August 24. The aircraft left Fairford at 5.33pm the following day and arrived at Dover Air Base in Delaware at 7.44pm local time before continuing to Chicago.The aircraft had not flown to RAF Fairford for at least two months before the incident, according to the reports.The US embassy confirmed it was investigating allegations involving a person assigned to the embassy but did not disclose the diplomat’s identity.“The United States government expects all personnel to adhere to the highest standards of conduct, and we take these allegations seriously,” an embassy spokesman said.The embassy said it had “quickly informed UK law enforcement and took swift action” and would continue working with British authorities.“The individual in question has been reassigned to the United States in conjunction with an ongoing investigation,” the spokesman said.The British Government said foreign diplomats were expected to comply with UK laws.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Amit Shah says decolonising knowledge not about erasing history, but reclaiming India's narrative
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said decolonisation of India's history and knowledge does not mean erasing the past, but presenting.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said decolonisation of India's history and knowledge does not mean erasing the past, but presenting historical truth authentically and from an Indian perspective.Shah made the remarks while inaugurating the 'Ganesh Gyanarthi' exhibition at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai. He said India's knowledge traditions, manuscripts and archives should be preserved and taken to people across the country and the world.“Decolonisation does not mean erasing history. From our perspective, it means presenting historical truth to the world in an authentic manner and from an Indian perspective,” Shah said, as cited by news agency PTI.He said the British had intertwined knowledge and power and argued that the task now was to free knowledge from that framework.“Today, we are moving forward to liberate knowledge from that and towards decolonisation,” Shah said.‘True knowledge is never held hostage by an ideology’Shah said knowledge should remain free from ideological constraints and criticised the colonial interpretation of India's intellectual traditions.“True knowledge is never held hostage by an ideology. Knowledge itself is an ideology. If you bind it in any way, you change the very meaning of knowledge. Knowledge should be free and uninhibited, and its declaration should also be free and uninhibited,” he said, according to ANI.“India's knowledge was not being written in India's voice. India's knowledge was being written in the language of a colonial perspective,” Shah said.He said the focus should now be on using the wealth and collections preserved at the Asiatic Society for the creation of a “Great India”.“Rather than going into why the Asiatic Society was formed, who formed it, and for what purpose, we should move forward in the direction of how the wealth, knowledge, and collections gathered here can be used in the creation of a Great India (Mahaan Bharat),” he said.Shah highlights manuscripts, proposes wider knowledge networkShah highlighted the rare manuscripts preserved at the Asiatic Society, including an illustrated copy of the Mahabharata and texts related to Jainism and Buddhism.“A great deal of things are lying here, including an illustrated copy of the Mahabharata. Such texts of Jain Kalpasutra and Buddhism are hardly available anywhere else; such texts are lying here. Much knowledge is present here that should have come out a long time ago,” he said.Shah called on the new committee to expand the institution's reach by bringing scholars from Maharashtra and across India to study its collections. He also proposed bringing libraries and institutions preserving heritage across the country onto a common platform under the Asiatic Society.He suggested creating a shared pool of knowledge that could be made available to students, researchers and scholars.Shah further proposed a campaign to collect ancestral documents preserved in villages and households across Maharashtra and link them with the Gyan Bharatam manuscript survey.“Because within these manuscripts lies immense knowledge, and there is a need to conduct research on this knowledge. A great power to take the nation forward lies within them,” he said.Referring to Nalanda, Shah said attempts to destroy physical repositories could not eliminate knowledge preserved through memory and tradition.“One can burn the library of Nalanda... but the knowledge that resides in people's minds as memory and tradition (Smriti and Shruti)—no one can destroy that knowledge,” he said.Shah said the Asiatic Society should work with the government and institutions across India to preserve and share India's knowledge traditions. He urged the new team to use Indology for the welfare of the country and the wider world.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rajasthan SET 2026: Students boycott exam in Jaipur over delayed papers, alleged irregularities
articles.summary: India News: Students walked out of a Rajasthan State Eligibility Test (SET-2026) centre in Jaipur on Sunday after alleging that question papers were distributed n.
articles.body: Students walked out of a Rajasthan State Eligibility Test (SET-2026) centre in Jaipur on Sunday after alleging that question papers were distributed nearly 30 minutes after the scheduled start, triggering protests and a boycott over what they described as serious exam irregularities.The disruption took place at Pink City Senior Secondary School on Bainar Road, where candidates said the exam was due to begin at 11am. They alleged that the question papers did not reach the centre until around 11.30am. Several candidates then left the centre and protested outside.The candidates also alleged that they were asked to either enter the examination hall and remain quiet or leave when they questioned officials about the delay.Anita Lamba, one of the candidates, questioned whether the same leniency would be extended to students who reached an examination centre even a minute after the gate-closing time."When we questioned the institution, they threatened us, saying that if we wanted to give the exam, we should go inside and sit quietly, or we could leave...This has been happening with children in the past, continues to happen, and will happen in the future," she told reporters.Candidates claim exam was cancelledThe situation escalated after candidates approached the police and raised their concerns with authorities present at the centre.Lamba said that after discussions with the police, the principal showed the candidates a notice stating that "the exam is being cancelled"."We have accepted the fact that the exam is cancelled," she said.However, there was no official notification confirming cancellation of the examination at the time of reporting.Another candidate, Sania Kaval, alleged that students were repeatedly asked to wait for five or 10 minutes as they waited for the question papers to arrive. When the papers eventually came, candidates were reportedly told that they would be given additional time to compensate for the delay."The invigilator at my centre was an 11th-grade student; she was signing papers as clumsily as a toddler might scribble. We asked why the paper hadn't arrived by 11:00 AM, and they told us it was on the way, asking us to wait for five minutes, then another ten minutes. The paper still didn't arrive, and when it came ten minutes late, they said we would get extra time...we want the cancelled exam to be held again, and second, we want this centre to be cancelled," she told ANI.Candidates said they ultimately agreed to appear for the examination after raising their concerns with the authorities. However, the delay and the manner in which the situation was handled led to a boycott by students at the centre.Exam irregularities have repeatedly triggered protestsThe Jaipur episode comes against a wider backdrop of repeated complaints over the conduct of competitive and government recruitment examinations in India. Delayed papers, question-paper leaks, impersonation, technical failures and allegations of administrative lapses have repeatedly led to cancellations, re-examinations and protests by aspirants.The Rajasthan Eligibility Examination for Teachers (REET) has previously been hit by question-paper leak allegations and other irregularities, while the state has also seen recruitment examinations disrupted by paper leaks and cheating allegations. The Rajasthan Police constable recruitment examination, for instance, had a paper leak controversy in 2022, leading authorities to cancel the affected paper and order a re-examination.For the SET candidates in Jaipur, the immediate demand is for clarity on whether Sunday's examination will stand or be cancelled. They have also demanded that the Bainar Road centre be removed from future examinations and that the test be conducted again if it is formally cancelled.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
